raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

This lets the DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 DSpark drafters use `draft_lm_head_quantization` (#59973), which so far was limited to EAGLE and MTP. A drafter that shares the target `lm_head` then computes its base logits through a private FP8 or NVFP4 copy of that head, while the target keeps verifying with its own BF16 head. It is the vLLM counterpart of sgl-project/sglang#39622.

```bash
vllm serve <model> --speculative-config \
  '{"method": "dspark", "num_speculative_tokens": 5, "draft_lm_head_quantization": "fp8"}'
```

## Claims

- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on MI355X, AgentX, `"fp8"`: ITL P50 is 4.0% lower at TP2 c1 and 2.4% lower at TP4 c1. A trace shows the draft-head GEMM going from 348 µs to 60 µs per step. From c8 up the result is neutral within noise.
- Acceptance length and GSM8K are unchanged within run-to-run noise, because the target still verifies with its own head.
- No new mechanism: the sharing logic EAGLE and DSpark had in common is now one helper, `share_target_lm_head`, and DSpark opts in through `DSparkSpeculatorConfig.supported_options`. Off by default.

## Validation

All runs: MI355X, `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-edad8b03` (the same vLLM commit as this PR's base) with the changed files mounted, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, InferenceX recipe `dsv41flash/vllm/mi355x-fp4-mtp/agentic.yaml` (DSpark k=5, probabilistic drafting, `--monokernel`). The only difference between arms is `"draft_lm_head_quantization": "fp8"`.

**AgentX** (InferenceX `infx.bench agentic`, golden synthetic AL 3.51, 900 s, fresh server per point, one run per point). ITL P50 in ms, BF16 head -> FP8 head:

| | c1 | c2 | c4 | c8 | c16 | c32 | c64 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP2 | 1.89 -> 1.81 (**-4.0%**) | 1.90 -> 1.81 (-4.9%) | 1.95 -> 1.86 (-4.5%) | 2.26 -> 2.24 (-0.7%) | 3.13 -> 3.11 (-0.5%) | 4.67 -> 4.69 (+0.4%) | 9.42 -> 9.35 (-0.8%) |
| TP4 | 1.56 -> 1.52 (**-2.4%**) | 1.57 -> 1.52 (-2.9%) | | | | | |

The c1 numbers match the trace below. At c2 and c4 the trace accounts for only about 0.5% (44 µs per step at c4), so most of the improvement measured at those points is run-to-run variance.

**Draft-head kernel per decode step** (torch profiler, TP2, rank 0, 60 steps). The draft-head GEMM is swapped one for one, and the target verify head (`Cijk_..._BBS`, about 104 µs) is untouched:

| | BF16 head | FP8 head |
|---|---|---|
| c1 (M=5) | `wvSplitK_hf_sml` 347.8 µs | `Cijk_..._F8BS` 54.6 µs + per-token quant 5.0 µs |
| c4 (M=20) | `Cijk_..._BBS` 104.5 µs | `Cijk_..._F8BS` 55.8 µs + per-token quant 5.0 µs |

**Acceptance and accuracy** (TP2, `rejection_sample_method: block`):

| | BF16 head | FP8 head |
|---|---|---|
| AL, AgentX traces at c8 (from `vllm:spec_decode_*` counter deltas, about 112k drafts each) | 3.416 | 3.400 |
| GSM8K 5-shot, all 1319, greedy, 2 runs | 0.909 / 0.913 | 0.904 / 0.914 |

**Tests** (MI355X, rebased branch): `pytest tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_omni.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_draft_lm_head.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_custom_speculator.py`: 54 passed, 4 skipped (the NVFP4 cases, which are CUDA-only). `pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/qwen3_5/test_mtp.py::test_mtp_draft_lm_head_quantization`, which exercises the refactored EAGLE/MTP path with `"fp8"`: passed. `pre-commit run --from-ref upstream/main`, including mypy: passed.

<details>
<summary>Full AgentX table, draft-head microbenchmark, run notes</summary>

| TP | conc | ITL mean/P50/P90 (ms) | output tok/s/GPU | TTFT mean (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 1 | 1.99/1.89/2.27 -> 1.92/1.81/2.26 | 78.6 -> 80.4 | 247 -> 242 |
| 2 | 2 | 2.02/1.90/2.30 -> 1.93/1.81/2.27 | 109.7 -> 109.2 | 249 -> 252 |
| 2 | 4 | 2.28/1.95/2.97 -> 2.11/1.86/2.41 | 137.6 -> 143.8 | 152 -> 140 |
| 2 | 8 | 2.50/2.26/3.64 -> 2.49/2.24/3.47 | 215.6 -> 212.9 | 140 -> 148 |
| 2 | 16 | 3.12/3.13/3.78 -> 3.17/3.11/3.78 | 336.3 -> 336.6 | 2030 -> 1999 |
| 2 | 32 | 5.03/4.67/6.02 -> 5.25/4.69/5.89 | 659.8 -> 661.8 | 6485 -> 6527 |
| 2 | 64 | 10.25/9.42/14.29 -> 10.05/9.35/14.19 | 1120.4 -> 1134.2 | 315 -> 321 |
| 4 | 1 | 1.61/1.56/1.80 -> 1.58/1.52/1.80 | 44.7 -> 44.9 | 189 -> 193 |
| 4 | 2 | 1.62/1.57/1.80 -> 1.60/1.52/1.81 | 56.6 -> 59.3 | 191 -> 207 |

At each TP2 point both arms ran at the same time on GPU pairs {2,3} and {4,5}, swapping pairs every point. The TP4 points ran one arm at a time on the same four GPUs. AgentX replays paced traces, so at low concurrency the arms serve different request mixes and token throughput follows that mix. ITL is the speed metric.

Draft-head GEMM alone (`ParallelLMHead` against `quantized_lm_head_copy`, CUDA-graph replay), in µs:

```
TP2 64640 x 5120   M=5    M=10   M=20   M=40   M=80   M=160  M=320
BF16               352.4  96.7   99.4   101.4  107.0  124.2  185.0
FP8                57.0   56.7   57.2   59.0   63.3   71.4   171.6
TP4 32320 x 5120
BF16               183.9  60.5   55.5   59.9   71.7   73.8   136.9
FP8                33.7   33.7   32.3   38.3   38.2   49.2   63.2
```

</details>

## Details

- **Changes**:
  - `share_target_lm_head` in `eagle/utils.py`, next to `_should_share`, installs the target head or its quantized copy, raises if quantization was requested but the drafter keeps its own head, and returns the installed head. `load_eagle_model` uses the returned head for the MTP `shared_head` fixup. `load_dspark_model` passes its vocab-size check as `can_share`. `load_dflash_model` can adopt it with `quantization=None` in a follow-up.
  - `DSparkSpeculatorConfig` accepts `draft_lm_head_quantization` only for `DSparkDraftModel` and `DSparkV41DraftModel`. Other DSpark drafters may read `lm_head.weight` directly: Muse Spark casts its activations to the head's dtype, which would be FP8 for a quantized copy. They are rejected during config validation, before the target loads. EAGLE's `head_dtype` check is shared through `check_draft_lm_head_quantization`.
  - Weight reload and weight transfer already refresh the copy, because `refresh_quantized_lm_heads` and `share_source_lm_heads` run on any `DraftModelSpeculator`.
- **Not a duplicate of #47584**: that PR adds a separate env var (`VLLM_DSPARK_FP8_DRAFT_HEAD`) and a new rowwise FP8 module, for the NVIDIA DeepSeek-V4 DSpark path only. This PR reuses the existing `draft_lm_head_quantization` config and kernel selection, so it works on any platform with an FP8 linear kernel.
- **Kernel on ROCm**: `"fp8"` resolves to `RowWiseTorchFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel` (hipBLASLt FP8 `_scaled_mm`).
- **Why c1 benefits most**: at M=5 (one request, five drafts) the BF16 dispatch picks `wvSplitK`, which is about 3.5x slower than at M=10. `deepseek_v41/amd/ops/draft_lm_head.py` already pads around that, but only on gfx942. A lossless fix to that dispatch is a separate follow-up.
- **Memory**: one extra FP8 copy of the per-rank head shard, about 0.33 GB at TP2 and 0.17 GB at TP4 for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. It is created during model loading, so KV sizing accounts for it.
- **CI coverage**: the quantized copy and its refresh are covered by the existing `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_draft_lm_head.py`. The shared EAGLE/MTP path is covered by the MTP e2e test above. The DSpark path is validated end to end above. CI has no DSpark checkpoint test for it. `"nvfp4"` takes the same path but was not measured here.

---

<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/syncing-a-fork
@AMD-yanfeiwang @shen-shanshan could you clarify why is this not using `--quantization-config.targets` ? What is the reason to introduce `draft_lm_head_quantization`?

Hi @fxmarty-amd, `draft_lm_head_quantization` comes from #59973, so let me answer for it. `targets` does not cover this case today:
1. The EAGLE/MTP/DSpark drafters share the target's `ParallelLMHead`. A `targets` entry quantizes that module in place, so the target's verification head would also become FP8 and outputs would change. `draft_lm_head_quantization` builds a private quantized copy for the drafter and leaves the target's BF16 head untouched, so target outputs are unchanged.
2. `targets` resolves only `LinearBase` and `RoutedExperts` layers; a pattern matching `lm_head` raises `online quantization is not supported for ParallelLMHead`.

We could consider a drafter-scoped key in `targets` that maps onto the same copy path, in case we want a single quantization surface.

> draft_lm_head_quantization builds a private quantized copy for the drafter and leaves the target's BF16 head untouched, so target outputs are unchanged.

Thanks @stecasta! Makes sense, so existing `--quantization-config.targets` is not be expressive/flexible enough in case we have tied (shared) weights. `--quantization-config.targets '{"*draft_model.*.lm_head":"xyz"}'` should eventually be possible.

As there is work to extend online quantization for lm head (#62708, #63402, #61815), I think indeed centralizing the API under `--quantization-config` would be nice.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.
Hi @AMD-yanfeiwang, thanks for the contribution. One point inline.

This block is now the same as the one in `load_eagle_model` (`eagle/utils.py`), and `load_dflash_model` has a third copy without the quantization. Should we move it into a helper next to `_should_share`, e.g. `share_target_lm_head(draft_model, target_lm_head, quantization, can_share=True)` that installs the target head (or its quantized copy), raises if quantization was requested but the drafter keeps its own head, and returns the installed head? DSpark would pass its vocab-size check as `can_share`, and EAGLE would use the returned head for the MTP `shared_head` fixup. DFlash could adopt it too with `quantization=None`, but that can be a follow-up.

nodes.body:
This now admits every DSpark drafter, but `MuseSparkDSparkForCausalLM.compute_draft_logits` (vllm/models/muse_spark/common/dspark.py) does `hidden_states.to(self.lm_head.weight.dtype)`. When its head is shared (identical full-vocab heads pass `_should_share`), `lm_head` becomes the quantized copy whose `weight` is the FP8 `qweight`, so the activations would be cast to float8 before the per-token quant path. Either that errors or it silently corrupts the draft logits, and with an FP32 target head `_quantize_copy` instead fails only after the target has loaded.

Could you please reject quantization for such drafters, or narrow the claim to the DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 drafters you validated?
Done, I added share_target_lm_head(...) next to _should_share, and EAGLE and DSpark both use it now. I'll move DFlash over in a follow-up.

This now admits every DSpark drafter, but `MuseSparkDSparkForCausalLM.compute_draft_logits` (vllm/models/muse_spark/common/dspark.py) does `hidden_states.to(self.lm_head.weight.dtype)`. When its head is shared (identical full-vocab heads pass `_should_share`), `lm_head` becomes the quantized copy whose `weight` is the FP8 `qweight`, so the activations would be cast to float8 before the per-token quant path. Either that errors or it silently corrupts the draft logits, and with an FP32 target head `_quantize_copy` instead fails only after the target has loaded.

Could you please reject quantization for such drafters, or narrow the claim to the DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 drafters you validated?
Done, I added share_target_lm_head(...) next to _should_share, and EAGLE and DSpark both use it now. I'll move DFlash over in a follow-up.

@AMD-yanfeiwang @shen-shanshan could you clarify why is this not using `--quantization-config.targets` ? What is the reason to introduce `draft_lm_head_quantization`?

Hi @fxmarty-amd, `draft_lm_head_quantization` comes from #59973, so let me answer for it. `targets` does not cover this case today:
1. The EAGLE/MTP/DSpark drafters share the target's `ParallelLMHead`. A `targets` entry quantizes that module in place, so the target's verification head would also become FP8 and outputs would change. `draft_lm_head_quantization` builds a private quantized copy for the drafter and leaves the target's BF16 head untouched, so target outputs are unchanged.
2. `targets` resolves only `LinearBase` and `RoutedExperts` layers; a pattern matching `lm_head` raises `online quantization is not supported for ParallelLMHead`.

We could consider a drafter-scoped key in `targets` that maps onto the same copy path, in case we want a single quantization surface.

> draft_lm_head_quantization builds a private quantized copy for the drafter and leaves the target's BF16 head untouched, so target outputs are unchanged.

Thanks @stecasta! Makes sense, so existing `--quantization-config.targets` is not be expressive/flexible enough in case we have tied (shared) weights. `--quantization-config.targets '{"*draft_model.*.lm_head":"xyz"}'` should eventually be possible.

As there is work to extend online quantization for lm head (#62708, #63402, #61815), I think indeed centralizing the API under `--quantization-config` would be nice.
